Introduction:

Painesville Municipal Court is a municipal court serving Lake County, Ohio residents. The court was established in 1840 when Painesville became a county seat. This court is known as a leader of the Ohio municipal court due to the provision of justice, innovation, the efficiency of finances, service and protection for public safety.

They provide fair, timely and cost-effective disposition in all matters appropriately presented in the court. The staff will treat every person in a proper and justice manner. This court has jurisdiction over criminal, probation, traffic, vehicle, small claims, bailiff and civil cases. This court also serves many agencies, including Concord Township Zoning, Headland Beach Park, Ohio Bureau of Employment, Ohio Department of Public Safety and Perry Township Zoning, etc. Proper dressing and masks are required when any person comes to the court.

How to do a case search?

Painesville Municipal Court case search can be found online using https://www.pmcourt.com/recordSearch.php?k=acceptAgreementsearchForm4320.The court maintained all the case records in the file or database. The case search can be done in the following ways:

  • Searching by case number
  • Searching by name/company
  • Searching by citation or ticket number
  • Searching by hearing date

Enter the case type you want to search. You can also manage matches per page in your case searches. After you enter any search-type information, it will come if it is available and is not confidential and sealed. If the case is personal and sealed, then you have to go to the court and request record access, and then the court will decide whether to provide that case information or not. Fees for the copies per page for records are mandatory, and you had to pay when coming to the court. The cost for the sealing records request is $50.

How to search for dockets?

Painesville Municipal Court dockets can also be found online using the calendar search https://www.pmcourt.com/hearingSchedule.php. Enter the beginning and ending date, the case types you want to search for and the matches per page. The detailed case schedule with the information will be displayed on your screen. Only confidential information is not available online; you must go to court for that type of information.

How to make a payment?

Painesville Municipal Court payment can be made in the following ways:

In-Person:

A person can pay tickets and fines by visiting the hall of justice during regular court hours and paying in cash, checks, U.S. funds, or a card at the court payment office. Take your ticket and case number with you when you come for payment. 2% surcharges will be applied if you make payment with a credit card.

Online:

Online payments can be made using https://www.pmcourt.com/payments.php?showItem=step_search-page&agencyNumber=4320&tempId=. Enter your last and first name, date of birth and O.L. number and click on search. The case with the payment amount will be displayed on the screen; pay with any online payment method. Convenience fees will be applied using this method.

Mail:

A Person can send a certified check or money order to the court's mailing address; Painesville Municipal Court, 7 Richmond St. P.O. Box 601, Painesville, OH 44077. Cash or personal checks are not acceptable in the mail; only certified checks or money orders are accepted. Remember to write your citation, name, case number, and account number when you send the payment, and mail the amount in a self-addressed, stamped envelope if you want a receipt. Please attach the courtesy notice to the envelope if paying for a traffic ticket.

Phone:

Payment can also be paid by calling the call centre of the court at 866-895-0198. Follow the steps they tell you. Service charges are applied in this case.

The traffic court handles which types of cases?

Painesville Municipal traffic court handles traffic and vehicle violations that include speeding, driving without or with an expired license, driving while having drugs, accidents, using a phone while driving, driving without seat belts, passing by school bus, motor vehicle reckless operation etc. The court will mail you a courtesy notice on the citation address after you receive a traffic or infraction ticket.

That notice will tell you detailed information on the citation number, schedule, violation you had done, bail amount, eligibility for traffic violation school etc. If your citation includes a court appearance, then appearing in the court on the schedule is mandatory. Many options for resolving traffic tickets if a court appearance is not required are:

  • Pay the total amount of the fine on time.
  • Show some proof of correction if the case is related to insurance or no vehicle registration and pay a reduced amount of fine with the correction fees.
  • Request for a court hearing and appear in front of the judge.
  • Enter a plea of not guilty and give a request for a trial by declaration

You had to respond with a solution before the deadline. Contact the clerk's office if you are still waiting to receive any mail for courtesy notice.

How to file a small claim case?

Painesville Municipal Court civil division handles small claim matters at most $6000. It is a special court where disputes and fights are solved inexpensively and quickly. The rules are very simple. You can file a complaint by filling out a form and sending it to the clerk's office. Fill in the personal information of the defendant and plaintiff, the brief reason for the claim and the amount you are claiming. All costs and forms related to small claims matters are available online at https://www.pmcourt.com/civil.php.

What is the responsibility of the bailiff department?

Painesville Municipal Court bailiff department is to provide security at this court and during the court proceedings. This department also had some other responsibilities that are subpoenas service, execution of some post-judgment, eviction notice serving and move out of the supervising. This department oversees vehicle immobilization; you can contact this court with any questions if your vehicle is seized.

How to schedule a wedding?

Painesville Municipal Court weddings can be scheduled by calling the marriage license bureau for the marriage license requirements or visiting https://www.lakecountyohio.gov/probate-court/marriage-department for the information. First, the license is made, and then the wedding is scheduled. The fee for the ceremony is $100, which will be paid at the time of the appointment. The wedding ceremony will be performed on Thursday after 10:45 am. You had to bring your photo I.D. and marriage license at the time of the ceremony.

FAQ:

How many fees had to be paid for the club removal in the court bailiff?

A $100 fee had to be paid to the bailiff department if you wanted to remove the club after the immobilization period.

What happens if I fail to appear or pay on time?

If you fail to appear or do not pay the fine on time, further conviction and fine will be imposed on you, your driving license and insurance will be suspended, and a $100 civil penalty will be imposed on you.

How can I see the active warrant list?

You can see all the active warrant lists online at https://www.pmcourt.com/activeWarrants.php. The case number, defendant name, agency, warrant issue date, and the reason for the issue will be available on this link.
